I’ve been a psych nurse a long time, so I know how this is going to sound, but for about a month I felt… almost unnaturally “up.” I was buzzing at work, doing double shifts, reorganizing the whole ward on my breaks, pacing all the time. I couldn’t sit through handover; I was constantly on the move, talking fast, taking on extra projects. It felt amazing, like I was the only one who really knew how to fix things, like I was the best nurse on the unit and could probably run the place better than management. I wasn’t sleeping much but didn’t feel tired—just wired.

Then about two weeks ago it flipped. I’ve been crying at the slightest thing—charting mistakes, a patient being transferred—and sometimes I have this overwhelming certainty that everything bad on the ward is somehow my fault: code blues, medication errors, even things on other shifts. I catch myself thinking I should just step off the hospital parking garage or walk into traffic on my way home. It’s not a detailed plan, more like these sudden urges that scare me. I’m divorced and live alone, and lately I can barely make it through a full shift.

I do feel a bit keyed up and anxious at times, but even when I’m not actually worried about anything, my thoughts are racing and I act on impulses—sending long emails at 3 a.m., taking on extra shifts, driving too fast.

Then I crash. For the last two weeks I’ve been crying at the slightest thing—med errors on the floor, a sad story on the news. I’m convinced I’ve harmed patients in ways that make no sense, like believing a bad outcome on another ward is somehow my fault. I’ve had sudden urges to just step into traffic after a shift or jump from the parking garage. I haven’t acted on them, but they scare me. I’ve called in sick several times because I just can’t function.

It’s constant—at work, driving home, even in the shower. The thoughts pile up so fast they feel like they’re racing, and then I get this urge to do something, anything—recheck charts, rewrite care plans, text my daughter repeatedly—just to quiet the anxiety.

When I try to sit still, I feel almost jittery inside, like I should be getting up to fix something I’ve forgotten. I keep overestimating what I can handle—extra shifts, extra responsibilities—because in the moment it feels like if I just do more, I’ll finally feel “caught up” and less anxious. But then I’m overwhelmed, exhausted, and end up crying in the medication room over tiny mistakes, blaming myself for every bad outcome on the ward, even when I know logically it’s not all on me. Some days I wake up feeling incredible, like I’m meant to be the best wedding planner in the city, like I’m supposed to change the whole industry. Then, in the middle of all that, I’ll suddenly snap at my husband or my staff over tiny things, and I don’t even know why my mood flips so fast.

But then, about two weeks ago, things crashed. I’ve been crying at random times—at my desk, in the car, even during venue walkthroughs. I keep thinking I’m a fraud, that my clients would be better off with anyone else. It’s like I’m worthless, just pretending to be competent. I’ve actually mapped out how I could end things—where I’d do it, what I’d use. That scares me, but at the same time it feels disturbingly…organized.

All along, there’s this constant nervousness underneath—like a tight knot in my chest—about work, money, my marriage, everything. It’s hard to tell if the worry is causing all this or if it’s just another layer on top. I know it’s affecting my job; I’ve missed meetings, and my husband is asking what’s happening to me.
